function.description:
[exa] Read a webpage's full content as clean markdown. Use after web_search_exa when highlights are insufficient or to read any URL.

Best for: Extracting full content from known URLs. Batch multiple URLs in one call.
Returns: Clean text content and metadata from the page(s).
function.name: exa.web_fetch_exa

maxCharacters.description: Maximum characters to extract per page (default: 3000)

urls.description: URLs to read. Batch multiple URLs in one call.

function.description:
[exa] Search the web for any topic and get clean, ready-to-use content.

      Best for: Finding current information, news, facts, people, companies, or answering questions about any topic.
      Returns: Clean text content from top search results.

      Query tips:
      describe the ideal page, not keywords. "blog post comparing React and Vue performance" not "React vs Vue".
      Use category:people / category:company to search through Linkedin profiles / companies respectively.
      If highlights are insufficient, follow up with web_fetch_exa on the best URLs.
function.name: exa.web_search_exa

numResults.description: Number of search results to return (default: 10).

objective.description: Goal for this search turn; say which documents should rank first, which should be excluded, and what specific facts or figures to pull from them.

query.description: Natural language search query. Should be a semantically rich description of the ideal page, not just keywords. Optionally include category:<type> (company, people) to focus results — e.g. 'category:people John Doe software engineer'.

function.description:
[sandbox] Run JavaScript in your private macOS sandbox to work on the project. The code is the body of an async function: `return` a value to see it (a lone expression is returned as is), and use console.log for notes. Batch steps: one call can read, edit and verify. These functions are synchronous (await is optional) and throw an Error on failure:
list(): string[]  // every project file path, relative, sorted
glob(pattern: string): string[]  // e.g. "src/**/*.ts"; without / it matches file names anywhere
view(path: string, offset?: number, limit?: number): string  // numbered `N| ` lines, 200 by default
read(path: string): string  // raw text, at most 1 MiB
search(regex: string, path?: string): {path: string, line: number, text: string}[]  // grep -E; at most 200 matches, 50 per file
edit(path: string, find: string, replace: string, all?: boolean): {line: number, count: number, snippet: string}  // `find` once (all: each); tolerates indentation, `N| ` prefixes, curly quotes
edits(path: string, changes: [find: string, replace: string][]): {count: number, lines: number[]}  // several edits of one file, all or nothing
write(path: string, text: string): void  // creates folders, at most 1 MiB
run(command: string): {status: number | null, stopped: boolean, omitted: number, output: string, job?: number}  // /bin/sh in the project, with Internet (curl, git clone, pip, npm); still running after 5 s: status null, continues as job `job`; output over 32 KiB keeps its first 8 and last 24 KiB, all of it in the file the result names
spawn(command: string): number  // background job (server, build), ≤4 at once, ≤15 min; its end is announced in a later result
jobs(): {id, command, running, status, seconds}[];  tail(id, lines = 40): string;  wait(id, seconds?): {id, running, status, seconds, output};  kill(id)
fetch(url: string): {status: number, url: string, type: string, text: string}  // HTTPS GET to the allowed hosts (*), text only, at most 2 MiB; redirects are checked
download(url: string, path: string): {status: number, url: string, bytes: number}  // saves into the project, at most 100 MiB; put test material under .mlxl3-scratch/ (never part of the reviewed changes)
The JavaScript itself has no direct network, files outside the project, require/import or timers. Limits per call: 10 s, 200 function calls, 32 KiB of output. `$` keeps any value between calls (emptied if the kernel restarts; a result says so). `state` is also kept on disk (JSON values, 256 Ki characters). Writing is enabled. A file's content goes in the `text` argument, not in the code: write(path, text) then needs no escaping.
function.name: sandbox.javascript

code.description: JavaScript, the body of an async function

text.description: Optional raw text (a file's content), read in the code as the variable `text`
